title: Short Stuff: Waffle House Index
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Waffle House Index, a informal FEMA disaster-assessment gauge based on whether a Waffle House is open, closed, or serving a limited menu after a storm. The hosts cover Waffle House's disaster preparedness: generators, a limited emergency menu, temporary food storage, a disaster playbook started after Hurricane Katrina in 2005, and "jump teams" that reopen locations quickly. Craig Fugate, FEMA administrator in the early 2010s, is credited with the idea after the 2011 Joplin tornado and hurricanes. The index uses green (fully open), yellow (limited menu, likely generator), and red (closed, so responders should go there first). A Hurricane Irene story from Wallace, North Carolina (2011) about cooking by gas-fed grill until dark is told. The episode also includes off-topic banter about personal food orders, a movie, and the hosts' childhood TV.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Short Stuff

segments.title: Opening banter and Waffle House overview
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Waffle House Index as a topic split from a planned full Waffle House episode, describe the chain's 24/7 reputation, and its disaster-response role. They trade personal anecdotes about ordering food there.

segments.title: Waffle House disaster preparedness plan
segments.summary: After Hurricane Katrina in 2005, Waffle House created a written disaster plan covering generators, a limited emergency menu, temporary food storage, and local storage options. Other companies, such as Lowe's and Home Depot, also play a role in post-disaster recovery.

segments.title: Origin of the Waffle House Index
segments.summary: Craig Fugate, FEMA administrator, came up with the idea after the 2011 Joplin tornado and several hurricanes. He noticed Waffle House was often one of the only businesses open, and used this to judge damage severity. The index uses three colors: green for fully open, yellow for a limited menu, and red for closed.

segments.title: How red-status locations are used
segments.summary: A closed Waffle House signals the hardest-hit community, where FEMA should send responders first. Waffle House usually reopens as soon as it is safe after evacuation orders.

segments.title: Hurricane Irene story and mobile command center
segments.summary: During Hurricane Irene in 2011, a Waffle House in Wallace, North Carolina lost power but kept its gas grill running until it got too dark, then reopened at dawn. The hosts also discuss a Waffle House mobile command center, which they could only find as a food truck, and mention the EM50 vehicle from the movie Stripes.

segments.title: Closing banter and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the movie Stripes and some personal memories, then close the Short Stuff episode with a reminder about the Waffle House Index and a mention of Kid Rock.
